descriptions.short: Hugo is one of the most popular open-source static site generators. With its amazing speed and flexibility, Hugo makes building websites fun again. This extended version allows native Sass compilation.
descriptions.long: Hugo is a static HTML and CSS website generator written in Go. It is optimized for speed, ease of use, and configurability. Hugo takes a directory with content and templates and renders them into a full HTML website. Hugo relies on Markdown files with front matter for metadata, and you can run Hugo from any directory. This works well for shared hosts and other systems where you don’t have a privileged account. Hugo renders a typical website of moderate size in a fraction of a second. A good rule of thumb is that each piece of content renders in around 1 millisecond. Hugo is designed to work well for any kind of website including blogs, tumbles, and docs. NOTE: : This package does not include the deploy feature. If you need this, see the hugo-extended-withdeploy package. NOTE: : This extended version allows native Sass compilation. NOTE : This is an automatically updated package. If you find it is out of date by more than a week, please contact the maintainer(s) and let them know the package is no longer updating correctly.

links.releases:
## Notable new features

* New [`imaging.firstFrameOnly`](https://gohugo.io/configuration/imaging/#firstframeonly) option (and a matching processing flag) to only decode/encode the first frame of animated images. Hugo now also only decodes the first frame when the target format doesn't support animation, and fails early with an informative error if processing all frames would exceed the WASM memory limit.
* New [`FrameCount`](https://gohugo.io/methods/resource/framecount/) method on images, e.g. to check if an image is animated.
* [`site.Language`](https://gohugo.io/methods/site/language/) now has `Translate` and `Format*` methods, so you can e.g. range over `site.Languages` and translate into each language.
* New `charset` option for [`js.Build`](https://gohugo.io/functions/js/build/) and [`css.Build`](https://gohugo.io/functions/css/build/).
* Basic support for the OSC 7501 program status (working/done/idle/error) in terminals that support it, alongside the existing OSC 9;4 progress.

## Security fixes

This release is built with Go 1.27.2, which includes [15 security fixes](https://seclists.org/oss-sec/2026/q4/101). The most relevant for Hugo are:

* Two `html/template` escaping fixes, which also apply to Hugo's fork of the package: [CVE-2026-94448](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/81821) (context tracking not reset on consecutive expressions in JS template literals) and [CVE-2026-97030](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/81823) (`yield` not recognized as a regexp preceder keyword). Both could lead to incorrect escaping of inline JavaScript.
* Several `net/http` fixes (HTTP/2 server crash and memory exhaustion, connection desynchronization, unbounded `Range` header parsing), relevant for `hugo server` and remote resources. The corresponding HTTP/2 fixes are also included via the upgrade of `golang.org/x/net` to v0.61.0.
* [CVE-2026-56857](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/81739): `os.Root.Mkdir(All)` could follow junctions out of the root on Windows.

Also:

* `github.com/tdewolff/minify` is upgraded to v2.24.19, which fixes [GHSA-3ppm-p7r9-c5w3](https://github.com/tdewolff/minify/releases/tag/v2.24.18): `</script>` (and `<!--`) inside inline scripts was not properly escaped (case-insensitively) when minifying JS in HTML.
* Hugo now ignores `module.replacements` defined in themes; only the project can define replacements.

* warpc: Upgrade to wasi-sdk-34 2f2f33b2 @bep 
* ci: Drop extended build tag on Windows tests 53aae446 @bep 
* Add imaging.firstFrameOnly and some animation performance improvements 13ee7e97 @bep #15433 
* js, css: Add charset option to js.Build and css.Build 0688a8cd @bep #15435
